children: AstraZeneca PLC (LSE:AZN) reported mixed clinical news: robust positive Phase 3 and Phase 2 results across COPD (tozorakimab), HER2‑mutant NSCLC (ENHERTU), TAGRISSO long‑term survival and Imfinzi+tarlatamab, alongside a failed SERENA‑4 trial, while CEO Pascal Soriot warned MFN pricing risks R&D cuts.
: AstraZeneca (AZN) reported Phase 3 tozorakimab trials (~2,306 patients): 29–34% fewer annual moderate-to-severe COPD exacerbations, ~36% fewer severe events, no new safety signals; PDUFA Q1 2027.
: AstraZeneca's ENHERTU showed DESTINY-Lung04 first-line HER2-mutant NSCLC PFS 14.3 vs 8.3 months (HR 0.63, p<0.0001); ORR 70.0% vs 44.5%; median DOR 13.4 vs 9.7 months; ILD/pneumonitis 20.8%.
: AstraZeneca’s AZN: ADAURA eight‑year results for TAGRISSO show OS reduction in death risk — Stages II–IIIA HR 0.53 (74% vs 58% alive) and IB–IIIA HR 0.52 (79% vs 64%); no new safety signals
: AstraZeneca’s AZN: Phase III DeLLphi-305 (563 patients) — Imfinzi + tarlatamab improved overall survival, progression‑free survival and response rate versus Imfinzi alone; no new safety signals.
: AstraZeneca (AZN) reported the SERENA-4 Phase III trial of Etcamah plus palbociclib failed to meet its primary endpoint. No details on secondary endpoints, timelines or next steps were provided.
: AstraZeneca (AZN) CEO Pascal Soriot warned U.S. most-favored-nation pricing could cut profits, trim R&D budgets, and limit clinical trials and new drug sales in Japan.

title: Weekly Recap: Tozorakimab cuts COPD events and ENHERTU improves PFS
